description:
🔴 **A story is marked passing when the agent says COMPLETE and any commit exists — its acceptance criteria are never read. Five stories in ONE DAY (2026-08-16/17) reported green against criteria that were not met.**

`driver.sh` is explicit about it:

```bash
# Trust an explicit COMPLETE from an agent that DID commit real work: mark any
# stories it left stale-false as passed so the branch proceeds to the verify
# gate (verify — not the pass-flags — is the real merge bar).
if [ "$agent_rc" = "0" ] && [ -n "$has_work" ]; then
  jq '.userStories |= map(.passes=true)'
fi
```

`gen.sh` validates that `acceptanceCriteria` is a non-empty array of strings **at authoring time** and nothing reads it again.

**The five, all with well-written, falsifiable criteria:**

| story | criterion | what happened |
|---|---|---|
| `cuneiform:346`/US-3 | file `argos:82` to `completed/` | still active |
| `cuneiform:347`/US-1 | an export declaring no extensions renders BYTE-IDENTICALLY | it did not render at all |
| `cuneiform:347`/US-4 | unpark `argos:90`, answer the separability question | neither done |
| `cuneiform:348`/US-2 | reach GREEN acceptance, baseline 77 failed | reached 25 failed |
| `insimul:164` | — | restarted at 0/3 with work committed |

**The cheapest available signal is already in the data: 9 of 10 passing stories across `346`/`347`/`348` have EMPTY `notes`.** A story that did its work has something to say about how; one that was force-passed has nothing.

**Two structural causes, and they need different answers.** First, criteria naming a path OUTSIDE the worktree cannot be satisfied there — `346`/US-3 and `347`/US-4 both asked a cuneiform worktree to edit `argos/tasks/`, which `cuneiform:313`'s US-FOLD had already identified as a boundary. Second, criteria stating a MEASURABLE BAR ("the baseline to beat is 77 failed") were reported met without the measurement being taken.

**Do not simply invert the force-pass.** The design reasoning — verify is the real merge bar — is sound, and an agent that genuinely finished should not be blocked by a stale flag. The goal is that a story cannot claim a *specific, checkable* thing and pass without it, not that chief becomes a second test runner.

userStories.title: A passing story must say how — empty evidence is not a pass
acceptanceCriteria: A story force-passed by the COMPLETE path must carry evidence in `notes`; an empty `notes` on a story the agent did not itself mark passing FAILS the run rather than merging. 9 of 10 passing stories across the three tasklists reviewed had empty notes, so this alone would have caught all five cases.

The requirement is on stories chief force-passes, NOT on stories an agent explicitly marked passing with its own reasoning — the point is to stop silent promotion, not to add ceremony to work that reported itself honestly.
The failure message names the story and quotes the criterion, so an operator sees WHAT was claimed rather than that a count did not match.
userStories.notes: Added evidence_gate()/unverified_stop() to engine/driver.sh: the COMPLETE path now promotes a stale-false story only when its `notes` are non-empty, leaves the rest false, and stops the branch as UNVERIFIED with the story id, title and each claimed criterion printed verbatim (ordered before the INCOMPLETE arm so the two failures stay distinguishable). Stories the agent marked passing itself are untouched. Proven by test/evidence-gate.sh (two tasklists, one run): ev-bad -> UNVERIFIED, not merged, not retired, message quotes both criteria; ev-good -> MERGED, so honest self-reported work pays no ceremony. Wired into test/all.sh and the .chief/verify.sh bystander subset; both green.

userStories.title: A criterion naming a path outside the worktree fails, loudly and early
acceptanceCriteria: An acceptance criterion referencing a path outside the run's worktree — a sibling repo like `argos/tasks/…`, or `../<repo>/` — is detected and FAILS the story, because it cannot be satisfied from where the run executes. Both `346`/US-3 and `347`/US-4 were structurally unsatisfiable and passed.
It is detected at AUTHORING time too: `chief gen` and a tasklist lint warn when a criterion names a cross-repo path, so the problem is caught when it is cheap rather than after a merge.

The escape hatch is explicit, not implicit — a tasklist that genuinely coordinates across repos can declare that, and the declaration is visible in the record. Silently allowing it is what produced these five.
userStories.notes: Added engine/criteria.sh — the scope rule in one place, shared by three callers so authoring time and run time cannot disagree. criteria_scope_report flags a criterion naming (1) `../<name>/…`, (2) chief's own `<repo>:<stem>` cross-repo notation (`argos:82`; the repo half may carry no dot, which keeps `driver.sh:1075` line refs out — a real false positive it caught on tasks/chief/97), or (3) `<repo>/…` rooted at a repo already established as foreign (tasklist text, cross-repo dependsOn, or a sibling checkout absent from the worktree). Severity matches what each caller can still do: `chief gen` WARNS and still generates, the new `chief lint` FAILS, and run_worker calls criteria_scope_stop right after seeding prd.json — status UNSATISFIABLE, event tasklist.unsatisfiable, story id+title, the offending token, the criterion quoted, and the hatch named, BEFORE the first agent turn. The hatch is explicit: "crossRepo":["argos"] on the tasklist (and a chief gen roadmap-item field, emitted only when declared). Proven by test/criteria-scope.sh (4 tasklists, one run): sc-ref (argos:82) and sc-path (argos/tasks/…) end UNSATISFIABLE with ZERO agent turns spent, unmerged and unretired; sc-declared (same criterion, declared) and sc-clean both MERGE; chief lint fails the undeclared one and passes the declared one; chief gen warns once and still generates with crossRepo carried through. Cost: one jq pass + one ls, once per tasklist per run (~30 ms), nothing during the agent loop. Regression scan over every tasklist in this repo (active + completed/) is clean except two genuine cross-repo citations. Full .chief/verify.sh green (25 hermetic tests under the bystander guard, doc-sync, version-bump, quality ratchet); VERSION 0.8.29 -> 0.8.30 with README in lockstep.

userStories.title: Measurable bars are measured
acceptanceCriteria: A criterion stating a checkable numeric or state bar — "reaches GREEN", "the baseline to beat is 77 failed", "exit 0" — requires the run to record the observed value beside the claim. `cuneiform:348` claimed a bar of 77-failures-to-green and delivered 25 failures while reporting 3/3.

Where chief cannot evaluate the bar, the story is marked `unverified` rather than `passes` — an honest third state, matching the rule the scoring metrics already use for claims that cannot be checked.

`docs/reference/verify-hook.md` records the division plainly: what chief enforces, what `.chief/verify.sh` enforces, and what remains a human's job. Chief's own comment says verify is the real merge bar; that is defensible, and it needs to be written where a tasklist author will read it.
userStories.notes: Added engine/measure.sh — the BAR rule, kept out of driver.sh so run_worker grew by exactly 1 line (function_length_max 440 -> 455, tol 15). measure_gate reads every story that ends the run PASSING (however it got there — chief promoted it or the agent marked it itself; a bar is a claim about a number and who typed the flag does not change that), fires when a criterion matches the closed bar list (exit/return 0|non-zero · green · byte-identical · "at least|no more than|under… N" · N% · "0 failures" · "N failed|passing|tests" · a baseline with a number) and the story's `notes` record no observed value, and then DEMOTES it: passes=false, unverified=true — the honest third state, the same rule chief quality already uses for a metric no analyzer could measure (unmeasured[] is skipped, never read as "nothing got worse"). unmeasured_stop fails the branch UNVERIFIED (same status + headless exit 6 as the evidence gate; the MESSAGE differs because the fix does) printing the story id+title, WHICH bar fired, the criterion verbatim and what the notes did say. Chief never judges whether the observation MEETS the bar — it cannot run another repo's suite — it only requires the number be written where a human can. Deliberately lenient on the evidence side (any number or result word passes) because a gate that fails honest work gets switched off. Runs on EVERY path to a merge, not only behind the agent-ran condition the evidence gate needs: the demotion lands in the runtime record while the committed tasklist still says passes:true, so the agent-free "all stories already pass — skip agent" resume would otherwise walk straight through the stop one run later. Proven by test/measured-bars.sh (2 tasklists, 3 fixture runs): mb-bad claims GREEN/77-failed and "exits 0", self-marks all 3 stories passing with a prose note, and ends UNVERIFIED with US-1+US-2 at unverified:true/passes:false, US-3 (states no bar) untouched at passes:true, nothing merged or retired, log naming both bars; mb-good ships the SAME criteria with "0 failed, down from the 77 baseline" in its notes and MERGES; a second run of mb-bad takes the skip-agent path and stops again. Calibration over this repo's 23 tasklists: 6 flag, 8 stories, every one of them with EMPTY notes and 5 of 8 genuinely unmeasured bars (the bare </>/≥ number rule was dropped after it fired on "≥1 tasklist ended VERIFY-FAILED"; the one residual false positive is a 40% quoted from a doc). Cost: one jq report + one jq rewrite per tasklist per run — 5 passes over the largest tasklist took 85 ms total (~17 ms each), nothing during the agent loop. docs/reference/verify-hook.md gained "Who checks what: chief, this hook, and you" — a three-layer table (engine / verify.sh / human) plus how to write criteria the engine can help with; tasklist-schema.md documents notes-as-evidence and the chief-written unverified field. Full .chief/verify.sh green: 26 hermetic tests under the bystander guard, doc-sync, version-bump, quality ratchet all OK; VERSION 0.8.30 -> 0.8.32 with README in lockstep.

userStories.title: Proven against the five that failed
acceptanceCriteria: Replaying the recorded shape of each of the five cases produces a FAILURE rather than a pass — as fixtures, not by re-running the original tasklists.

A story that genuinely met its criteria still passes: a regression suite over recent GREEN tasklists (`344`, `349`, `pinakes:104`) shows no new false negatives. A gate that fails honest work would be abandoned inside a week, which is the failure mode every gate added here has had to avoid.
The added cost is stated in the PR. This runs on every story of every tasklist, and a slow check gets disabled.
userStories.notes: Added test/five-cases.sh — one run, nine replayed tasklists, both halves together. THE FIVE, as fixtures carrying each case's deciding criteria verbatim and the agent behaviour its record shows (never re-runs — that would need three sibling repos and would prove today's code passes, not that the gate catches the shape): fc-346-us3 and fc-347-us4 end UNSATISFIABLE with ZERO agent turns spent, the log naming argos:82 / argos:90 and the crossRepo hatch; fc-347-us1 (renders **byte-identically**) and fc-348-us2 (GREEN acceptance, baseline 77 failed) end UNVERIFIED with the bar and the criterion quoted; fc-164 commits work and leaves 3/3 stories false with empty notes, and all three are reported by id. None of the five merged or retired. THE REGRESSION HALF, notes AS RECORDED: gr-344 (bars in its criteria, notes full of measured values) MERGED; gr-349 (no bar, EMPTY notes on all three stories, self-marked) MERGED with those empty notes intact — honest self-reported work pays no ceremony; gr-104-fix MERGED. THE ONE FALSE NEGATIVE, stated not hidden: pinakes:104 AS RECORDED is stopped — its criteria say "reports zero errors" and "stays green" and its filed record says nothing at all, so from the record chief cannot tell it from cuneiform:348, which claimed GREEN and delivered 25 failed. So the measured result is 2 of 3 clean as-recorded, 3 of 3 once the record carries its evidence; the remedy is ONE line of notes and gr-104-fix (identical criteria) proves it. Asserting the stop keeps it visible rather than letting it be rediscovered as a switched-off gate. The replay also found a real reporting gap in the headline case: measure_gate named only the FIRST bar, so 348/US-2 reported "GREEN" while its "77 failed, 860 passed, 39 errors" baseline fell past the 200-char clip — it now lists every bar the criterion states, and the real 348 record reports both. COST (criterion 3), measured over this repo's largest tasklist (12031 bytes, 4 stories, 13 criteria), 5 passes each: criteria_scope_report ~31 ms, measure_gate ~24 ms, evidence_gate one jq of the same order — ~55 ms per tasklist per run, none of it inside the agent loop, against runs measured in minutes; recorded in docs/reference/verify-hook.md under "What the engine layer costs, and what it was proven against", and the test itself asserts 5 combined passes stay under 5s so a future slowdown fails the test instead of being discovered as a disabled gate. Wall clock: the 9-tasklist fixture run takes 50s. Wired into test/all.sh and the .chief/verify.sh bystander subset; full verify green (27 hermetic tests, doc-sync, version-bump, quality ratchet). VERSION 0.8.32 -> 0.8.33 with README in lockstep.
